clue.text: Some foolish joke, hard to see at first but simple

indicators.note: says the hard letter is to be seen at the very front, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: a foolish arrangement of the letters of 'Some' is a muddled one

parts.note: a pun is a joke built on wordplay

explanation.surface: A silly gag is hard to get at first, though it turns out to be simple.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the pencil-grade mark for hard; 'to see at first' puts it at the very front before the muddled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun things are plain and unsophisticated, like cloth spun at home.

clue.text: Man touched drink with tongue

indicators.note: the two pieces touch, standing side by side

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
a brew is a drink such as tea or beer

explanation.surface: A man has wet his tongue with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrew is a language, and tongue is an old word for language.

clue.text: Quirk of Italian post-Renaissance style

explanation.surface: Some odd habit belongs to a style of Italian art after the Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal habit or affectation is a mannerism, and the same word names the sixteenth-century Italian art movement after the High Renaissance.

clue.text: Unwell, put on to water

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits on top of the first, so one is placed on to the other

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
unwell means sick

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill after being sent out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry, 'put on to' places SICK below SEA; the whole clue also describes being made ill by a boat trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nauseous from a vessel's motion is the very condition of feeling ill once set afloat.

clue.text: Tie with one hand

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
E for East, one of the four hands at a bridge table

explanation.surface: Someone ties a knot using only one hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so a 'hand' can be E.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie things together is to join or bind them as one.

clue.text: He's no longer in stable employment

definitions.text: He's no longer in stable employment

parts.words: He's no longer in stable employment
parts.note: reads as someone out of a steady job, but means a man whose work in horse stables at inns is a thing of the past

explanation.surface: A man who has lost his secure job.
explanation.definitionFit: The old inn servant who looked after travellers' horses is an obsolete trade, his work done in a stable.

clue.text: Determined to get result of hunt in the pot

indicators.note: the hunt's result goes inside the word for determined

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on doing something
the kill is the animal taken at the end of a hunt

explanation.surface: Someone is set on getting the day's game into the cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled cooking vessel, a small metal saucepan or frying pan, is a kind of pot.

clue.text: Pretend it's the fashion in Paris

parts.note: le is French for the, the phrase being set in Paris
ton is French for fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: Claiming something is the latest Parisian fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' puts both words into French: le ton, the fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on can mean to make out or feign, as in letting on that one is ill.

clue.text: Erred badly about Bottom being translated

indicators.note: the anagram goes about, around, the word for bottom
done badly, the letters of erred are jumbled

parts.note: the end is the bottom of something

explanation.surface: An actor playing Bottom got it badly wrong in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream whom Quince says is 'translated' into an ass, which gives the surface its theatrical gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered can mean put into another language, a synonym for converted from one tongue to another.

clue.text: Feeling better than expected about less than perfect course result?

explanation.surface: A golfer is in good spirits despite a scorecard that is not quite perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf par is the expected score for a course, so taking more strokes, a worse result, is over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling healthier than normal is being in good form beyond the norm, and on the golf links scoring more strokes than standard is a poorer round.

clue.text: Composer who worked closely with his peers, we hear

definitions.text: Composer who worked closely with his peers, we hear

parts.words: Composer who worked closely with his peers, we hear
parts.note: the English composer whose lifelong partner and collaborator was the tenor Peter Pears; 'his peers' sounds like 'his Pears'

explanation.surface: A composer who collaborated closely with his fellow musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The twentieth-century English composer of Peter Grimes partnered the tenor Peter Pears in life and work.

clue.text: One hiding away before having a child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone went into hiding before the baby arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or recluse withdraws from the world, hiding away from society.

clue.text: Curtain off enclave

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of enclave are out of order

explanation.surface: A curtain cuts off a small enclosed area.
explanation.definitionFit: A valance is a short drapery hung along the top of a window or bed, a kind of curtain.

clue.text: It's restorative to take a light vehicle round Maine

indicators.note: the vehicle goes round the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a pickup is a light truck with an open back
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: Driving a little truck around Maine is a refreshing tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic drink that perks someone up is a restorative.

clue.text: A balancing act — horsemanship does without it

indicators.note: the riding word goes without the word it, losing those letters

parts.note: equitation is the art of riding horses
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider manages a delicate balancing feat without help.
explanation.walkthrough: EQUITATION loses its IT to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics both sides of the expression must balance, a statement that two quantities are equal.

clue.text: Have a bit of sense

explanation.surface: Try a little bit to see what it is like.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample a little of food is to try it on the tongue, and flavour perception is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Rock single stands out at the top

indicators.note: in this down entry the anagram sits at the top, above the word for single
stands out reads as its letters put out of order

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: One lone rock stands out at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedimentary stone formed from compressed grains of sand is a rock.

clue.text: Fast, but such neat work

indicators.note: work suggests the letters of such neat are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Something quick, yet the work is very tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast in its old sense means loose in morals, the opposite of chaste.

clue.text: Turn back on meeting furious tribesman maybe

indicators.note: the word on is turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
mad means furious

explanation.surface: A furious tribesman turns back on meeting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home, such as a member of a roaming tribe.

clue.text: Heaven-sent nasal drip

parts.note: a drop of moisture falling from the sky at dawn, and also slang for a drop hanging from the end of a nose

explanation.surface: A runny nose that seems sent from above.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning moisture forms in small beads, and the same name is jokingly given to a drip at a person's nose.

clue.text: As student, is in group making revolution

parts.note: being up is being in residence at university

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the word for group

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student joins a group that is plotting revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is British for being at university, as in up at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt or rebellion against authority is a revolution.

clue.text: Sister put coins in jacket

indicators.note: the coins go inside the abbreviation for sister

parts.note: pence are British coins

explanation.surface: A nun slipped some coins into a jacket pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: A spencer is a short close-fitting jacket, named after an Earl Spencer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short waist-length coat worn in the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: Roman conspirator, non-U but cordial

indicators.note: non-U says the letter U is dropped from the conspirator's name

parts.note: Cassius was one of the plotters who killed Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A Roman plotter, not upper-class but friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is British slang for not upper-class, here read as 'without U'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackcurrant liqueur or syrup is a cordial.

clue.text: Such a one is damaged — unfortunate flaw within

definitions.text: Such a one is damaged — unfortunate flaw within

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go within the word for damaged

parts.note: hit can mean damaged, as with a town hit by a storm

indicators.note: an unfortunate flaw is a bungled one, its letters disordered

explanation.surface: A person who has suffered harm because of an unlucky defect inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone damaged by an unlucky defect in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish or simple-minded person is one thought to have only part of their wits.

clue.text: COming up, he may cause people to flee

definitions.text: he may cause people to flee

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to repel is to drive people away

explanation.surface: As he approaches, people run away.
explanation.walkthrough: Historically sufferers of leprosy were shunned, so the definition shares words with the wordplay as a semi-all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with leprosy was traditionally an outcast whom others avoided.

clue.text: Pensioners' bridge team

explanation.surface: Retired people form a bridge-playing team.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea Pensioners are the veteran soldiers of the Royal Hospital Chelsea in London; Chelsea Bridge crosses the Thames; Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A London district names the red-coated veterans' home, a Thames crossing, and a Premier League football club.

clue.text: Borrow an assortment of keys

explanation.surface: Asking to borrow a bunch of keys.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to get something from others without intending to return it, and C, A, D, G and E are each a musical key.

clue.text: Top musicians have no resistance in the cold

definitions.text: have no resistance in the cold
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the plural noun: materials that have no resistance at low temperature

parts.note: super means top, excellent
conductors are musicians who lead orchestras

explanation.surface: Leading musicians cannot cope with cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the things do; in physics such materials lose all electrical resistance near absolute zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain materials carry electric current with zero resistance when chilled to very low temperatures.

clue.text: Continent line introduced by Evangelical Union

parts.note: EU is the abbreviation for Evangelical Union
a rope is a line, a cord

explanation.surface: A continental line of thought brought in by a church union.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the world's great land masses, west of Asia.

clue.text: Relishes working without children

indicators.note: working shows the letters of relishes are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys their job and has no kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no offspring means having no one to inherit.
